title: Integral closure of a Noetherian domain in a finite fraction-field extension has Noetherian spectrum
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] which is an integral domain, meaning $1\ne0$ and $ab=0$ implies $a=0$ or $b=0$. Let $K=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ be its fraction field, namely the field of quotients $a/b$ with $a,b\in A$ and $b\ne0$. Let $L/K$ be a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] of finite degree, meaning that $L$ is finite-dimensional as a $K$-vector space. Let $B$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $L$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], with $A\to L$ the composite through $K$. Then the Zariski topological space underlying $\operatorname{Spec}B$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is Noetherian: every nonempty collection of closed subsets has a minimal member for inclusion. No module-finiteness or Noetherian-ring hypothesis on $B$ is assumed. In particular this applies to $L=K$.

source.place: W. Heinzer, Minimal primes of ideals and integral ring extensions, Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 40 (1973), 370–372, Theorem 2, printed pp. 371–372, specialized to the integral closure in a finite fraction-field extension; for L=K, the Corollary on p. 372. Theorem 2 assumes a Noetherian integral domain, not merely a domain with Noetherian spectrum. Printed article text read online from the author-uploaded ResearchGate copy, https://www.researchgate.net/publication/243057689_Minimal_primes_of_ideals_and_integral_ring_extensions (DOI 10.1090/S0002-9939-1973-0319962-X). WANTED: PDF absent from the local literature collection.

proof.text: Fix the given Noetherian domain $A$. For each prime $\mathfrak p\subset A$, let $N(\mathfrak p)$ assert: for every finite field extension $F/\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak p)$ and every subring $C\subseteq F$ containing $A/\mathfrak p$ and integral over it, $\operatorname{Spec}C$ has descending chain condition on closed subsets. Prove all $N(\mathfrak p)$ by induction towards larger primes. Such induction is legitimate: in any ascending chain of ideals the union is an ideal; its finitely many generators lie in one term, so the chain stabilizes by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Thus a nonempty set of counterexample primes has a maximal member. Fix $\mathfrak p$, assuming $N(\mathfrak q)$ for every $\mathfrak q\supsetneq\mathfrak p$. Set $R=A/\mathfrak p$; it is a domain and is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-image-noetherian]. The assertion is vacuous when there are no $C,F$ under consideration. If $\mathfrak p$ is maximal, $R$ is a field and an integral domain algebra $C$ over $R$ is a field: a minimal-degree monic relation for $0\ne c$ has nonzero constant term and expresses $c^{-1}$ as a polynomial in $c$. Then its spectrum is one point, giving the induction base.

source.place: Tag 00FM, section-Noetherian; Tag 00FN, lemma-Noetherian-permanence. Explicit ascending-chain induction and field base case; agent proof.

proof.text: Take $F,C$ in $N(\mathfrak p)$ and let $D$ be the integral closure of $R$ in $F$. By [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], $R\subseteq C\subseteq D\subseteq F$ and every element of $D$ is integral over $R$. If $Q\subset D$ is a nonzero prime, choose $0\ne x\in Q$ and a monic relation of least degree for $x$ over $R$. Its constant coefficient $a_0$ is nonzero: otherwise cancel $x$ in the domain $F$ to obtain a smaller-degree monic relation. The relation gives $a_0=-x(x^{d-1}+a_{d-1}x^{d-2}+\cdots+a_1)\in Q\cap R$. Consequently the inverse image $\mathfrak q\subset A$ of $Q\cap R$ is prime and strictly contains $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tags 00GI (integral elements) and 00GP (definition-integral-closure); the nonzero contraction is proved explicitly by a minimal-degree monic relation.

proof.text: For this nonzero $Q$, apply [lem-trf-almost-finite-residue-field-degree] to the Noetherian domain $R$, the finite field extension $F/\operatorname{Frac}(R)$, and its integral subring $D$. It says $E=\operatorname{Frac}(D/Q)$ is finite over $\operatorname{Frac}(R/(Q\cap R))=\operatorname{Frac}(A/\mathfrak q)$. The equality uses the ring isomorphism $A/\mathfrak q\to R/(Q\cap R)$ sending the class of $a$ to the class of $a+\mathfrak p$. Reducing a monic relation modulo $Q$ shows each element of $D/Q\subset E$ is integral over $A/\mathfrak q$. Since $\mathfrak q\supsetneq\mathfrak p$, the induction hypothesis $N(\mathfrak q)$ applies and gives Noetherian topology on $\operatorname{Spec}(D/Q)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-quotient-homeomorphism-zero-locus], this spectrum is homeomorphic to the closed subset $V(Q)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}D$, so $V(Q)$ is Noetherian.

source.place: Proposition 4.8.5, printed p. 85, supplies the finite degree; Stacks algebra.tex Tag 00E5, lemma-spec-closed, identifies the quotient spectrum. The use of induction and reduction of monic equations is written out.

source.place: Definition 4.10.1, Proposition 4.10.3 and Theorem 4.10.5 supply the principal-radical input. The finite-union and closed-subspace arguments are elementary and explicit.

proof.text: It follows that $\operatorname{Spec}D$ itself has descending chain condition on closed subsets. Indeed, given a descending chain, either every term is the whole spectrum or some term is proper. In the second case the remaining chain lies in that Noetherian closed subspace by Step 4 and therefore stabilizes. No ring-Noetherianity of $D$ is used.

The inclusion $C\hookrightarrow D$ is integral: each $d\in D$ satisfies a monic polynomial with coefficients in $R\subseteq C$, which is also such a polynomial over $C$. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over] gives a surjection $\operatorname{Spec}D\to\operatorname{Spec}C$. It is continuous by the spectrum construction [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. A descending chain of closed subsets of $\operatorname{Spec}C$ pulls back to a stationary chain in $\operatorname{Spec}D$ by Step 5; surjectivity makes equality of inverse images imply equality of the original subsets. This proves $N(\mathfrak p)$ for every $F,C$ and completes the induction.

source.place: Tag 00GQ, lemma-integral-overring-surjective, and functorial continuity of Spec; the descent of the closed-chain condition is explicit.

proof.text: Apply $N(0)$ with $F=L$ and $C=B$, using $A/(0)\simeq A$. The hypotheses hold because $A$ is a domain, $L/\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ is finite and $B$ is by definition the subring of elements integral over $A$. Thus the Zariski space of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is Noetherian. Descending chain condition is equivalent to the stated minimal-member property: a collection without a minimal member recursively supplies a strictly descending chain; conversely the distinct tail of a nonstationary descending chain has no minimal member. The degree-one extension $L=K$ is included.

source.place: Tag 0051, definition-noetherian; specialization and equivalence with the minimal-member formulation.

proof_origin.place: The seven-step Noetherian-prime induction is written explicitly here and checked against Heinzer, Theorem 2 proof (printed pp. 371–372), together with the principal-radical and finite-residue-degree inputs recorded as separate nodes. Heinzer proves the broader almost-finite-extension theorem by induction on generators and an ascending chain of contractions; the present induction on prime contractions is a faithful specialization route for the stated finite fraction-field integral closure.
